note: Story-telling deck for Hermes Scrollback Reel. The facts of every episode come from the user's own gated history; this deck only decides HOW an episode is framed and drawn, so a new chapter never looks or reads like the last one. Expanded 26/10/26 to 50+ entries per section at Sahil's request, with vocabulary informed by the local Midlibrary catalogue (art movements, techniques, camera modifiers, filmmakers); entries are our own phrasing, never catalogue text. Combinations = conflicts x worlds x genres x villains x motifs x shots.

cyberpunk chase: speed, neon, near-misses
quiet drama: small gestures, held silences, weight in the eyes

heist: a plan with moving parts and one detail nobody accounted for
siege: holding a line while resources drain
samurai tale: duty, a single cut, consequences outliving the blade
western standoff: dust, distance, who draws first
space opera: vast scale, one small decision that turns the fleet

coming of age: first failure, first mastery, a person taking shape

cosmic horror: scale beyond comprehension, sanity leaking at the edges
fable: a plain lesson told through objects, animals or weather
parable: a small story carrying a larger argument
myth: origins, trials, a figure who becomes a name
ghost story: old wrongs returning as cold drafts and unfinished business
whodunnit: suspects, alibis, the detail everyone walked past
courtroom drama: testimony, objection, the truth dragged into the open
war chronicle: fronts, supply lines, cost counted in people
road movie: movement, changing weather, talks that only happen in transit
buddy story: two temperaments welded together by one job

underdog sport: the long shot who does the unglamorous work

steampunk caper: brass, steam, an outrageous machine and a tidy plan

cyber noir: rain on chrome, a case that indicts the client
magical realism: one impossible thing accepted as ordinary
absurdist: rules that hold inside the frame and nowhere else
satire: the system shown at its own logic's end
farce: doors, timing, everything almost colliding
melodrama: feeling at full scale, stakes worn on the sleeve
tragedy: a flaw that could have been avoided and never was
requiem: something ends and is properly mourned
ballad: a story carried by rhythm, repeated lines, a refrain
